Adding a Detector

Source: vignettes/adding-a-detector.Rmd
adding-a-detector.Rmd

A detector is the smallest unit of extension in formex: a pure is_<type>() predicate that answers one yes/no question about each value. Adding a type means writing that predicate, proving it with a fixture, and wiring it into the registry and ontology so guess_data_type() can route to it. This guide walks the whole path with a worked example. It builds on vignette("detector-kinds") (what structure to key on) and vignette("autotype-framework") (how to prove it).

What a detector is

A predicate: character in, logical out, the same length, and it never errors on messy input.

is_ensembl_id <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  grepl("^ENS[A-Z]*[GTP][0-9]{11}$", x)   # ENSG/ENST/ENSP + 11 digits
}
is_ensembl_id(c("ENSG00000139618", "ENST00000407559", "not-an-id", NA))
#> TRUE TRUE FALSE NA

Missing values pass through as NA; nothing throws. That is the entire contract.

The six steps

1. Collect 10-25 positives

Real values, varied enough to cover the format’s range (different prefixes, lengths, edge cases).

P <- c("ENSG00000139618", "ENSMUSG00000102659", "ENST00000407559",
       "ENSP00000354587", "ENSG00000157764")

2. Build a fixture of positives + hard negatives

generate_autotype_test_cases() mutates the positives into S1/S2/S3/SP near-misses (see vignette("autotype-framework") for the tiers).

cases <- generate_autotype_test_cases(P, data_type = "ensembl_id")
table(cases$label)   #> valid + S1/S2/S3/SP negatives

3. Pick a strategy and write the predicate

Choose the tightest structure the type supports (vignette("detector-kinds") lists them: lookup, structured regex, regex+range, anchor+length, checksum). Ensembl IDs are a structured regex: a fixed prefix and an 11-digit body.

4. Score it and iterate

Run the detector against the fixture and read the recall / per-tier false-positive table. Tighten until recall is 1.00 and the structure-scramble tier SP is near 0.

res <- build_autotype_results(is_ensembl_id, P)
autotype_summary(res)              # recall + S1/S2/S3/SP pass rates
generate_autotype_report(res, "ensembl_id")   # the exact near-misses still passing

5. Wire it into the package

Four files, each touched once:

File Add
R/dt-<family>.R the is_<type>() function (here R/dt-scibio.R)
data-raw/datatypes/<family>.R the positive-example vector, named exactly <type>
R/00-data-type-registry.R one registry line: detector + human label
inst/extdata/research_data_type_ontology_v7.csv a row for the semantic type (its data_type/semantic_family/semantic_type and its formex recipe)

The registry line is what guess_data_type() and score_data_type() read; the ontology row is what lets the guess resolve to a semantic path and carry a stabilization recipe (see vignette("data-type-ontology") and vignette("formex")).

# R/00-data-type-registry.R
ensembl_id = list(detector = "is_ensembl_id",
                  label    = "Ensembl gene/transcript ID")

The example-vector name must match the registry key (ensembl_id), so the build script can pair positives with the detector automatically.

6. Rebuild the test bank and validate

Regenerate the frozen fixtures and check the ontology is still consistent.

# from the package root:
#   Rscript data-raw/build_test_cases.R        # refresh data_type_tests
#   fx_validate_ontology(fx_ontology())        # ontology integrity
guess_data_type(P)$route   # the new type should now resolve

A note on loose formats

Not every type can reach recall 1.00 / SP 0. A loose format (a bare integer code, a free-text-ish token) will leak negatives no matter how the regex is written — that is a true statement about the data, not a bug. vignette("detector-kinds") calls these out, and the honest move is to register the type at the depth its values actually support, letting the router’s name evidence and the verifier’s foil-selectivity gate do the rest, rather than forcing a brittle rule.
